reviews.reviewbody: All of these 77' shows sound great to me, and the quality on this one is very good, but could have better highs. 5 star show, 4 star recording. Cranking the treble to about 3:15 remedies the problem with the highs & turns a 4 star recording into a 5 star recording! Cranking the treble all the way creates a noticeable hiss, whereas at 3:15 the hiss disappears into the recording. You can still hear the hiss between songs or if you walk up to your speaker and listen out of your tweeter, but who cares, from a distance I don't hear any hiss except between songs and the quality is 5 stars! Awesome show too!

i mean, all you really have to look at is the setlists to figure this one out.  Any live show that has a Sunrise in it, is a damn good one since it was the only song that Donna sung correctly.  But the second set blows me away, the terrapin blows me away every time i listen to it, and that Miss. half step is on fire!! Jerry had  near perfect tone on his Travis Bean for this show, the notes seem to cut through the air. Kudos for this show, 5 stars without hesitation

oh, and an excellent Jack-A-Roe as well, worth a listen for sure

was playing the Wolf again in '77 as his regular axe.  My buddy was at the Bosyton show the night before Cornell and told me.  Soemone correct me if I am wrong here but the Bean did not get much use after '76.  Jerry was definitely using the Wolf at mnost of the '78 shows.

This is a great show, hot Scarlet>Fire, sweet first set High Time which was nice in any decade.

listen to "Passenger "  


without her it would of been as powerful/soulful

This tour never ceases to amaze! This was Donna's best tour by far, i really enjoy her vocal lead-ins to the scarlet jams on this tour (Richmond 5/25 is my personal fave). I searched this show on Dead.net and discovered the Jack-A-Roe is on Fallout from The Phil Zone. This tour and Europe '72 are my favourites. Of course with music, there is no right and wrong, but this show is All right to me!!!

Teabag,

Jerry didn't start playing the Wolf again until the Fall '77 tour. This is the TB500 Travis Bean. Check out this great website, tracking the history of the guitars Garcia used.

http://www.dozin.com/jers/guitar/history.htm

There's very little in this whole year that gets less than 5 stars and this show is no exception.

An early Jack-a-Roe with it's original funkier rhythm (I hate to admit it but I like the later, bluegrassy version better)and a gorgeous High Time in the first set.The second set run of Terrapin > Playing > Wharf Rat > Playing is fantastic. Check out this high energy Sugar Mag encore - Bobby just loses it.

gotta say
another winner

This show is definately a keeper, and is among the reasons that I would not be surprised that a Spring '77 tour boxed set comes out some day.

There is nothing at all to complain about this show except for one complaint I have about the entire Spring '77 tour altogether, and that is the aluminum neck that is on Jerry's TB500 Travis Bean...it sounds tinny to my ears, but he is playing to it and so that somewhat makes up for the tinny tone. I think the Spring '78 run, faults and all, *sounds* netter because Jerry is using Doug Irwin's Wolf guitar. It has a much warmer, richer tone to it.

But never mind me and my nit-picking...the Spring '77 tour can legitimately be called legendary.

5 stars, no questions asked.

Okay.  You are wrong about when Wolf was brought back. It was only in late December of 1977--the 29th, specifically, I believe. Wolf was "in the closet" for part of 75, all of 76, and the last few days of 1977. Then came Tiger.  Wolf came out, again, in 1989---with MIDI capabilities. Spring Tour 1977 was 100% Travis Bean.

Hey!  Check out the "Jack-a-Reggae".

An excellent offering from the spring of 1977, a period when the band was in sublime form. The highlight to me was the exquisite 10 minute jam  out of Estimated that segues into a joyful Eyes intro jam, which clocks 5 minutes even before Jerry sings the first verse. The recording: crisp and effervescent. The band took off at he end of 1974, and came back leaner with a faster tempo and less of the jazzy feel of 1974, yet they never forgot what they were great at.

Eyes through Stella is pure gold. Jerry is on a mission. A stand-out, middle-of-the-second-set jam from an overlooked show during month of stand-out shows.

I really can't say enough about the Stella Blue from this show. The transition from the Other One and the excruciatingly slow and luscious pace make this 15+ minute Stella an all-timer.

Besides disagreeing with the whole view that Brent brought more to the band than Keith and Donna, I find it most interesting that so many of us think the 1977 period was when the Dead were at their best. Certainly, a good argument can be made that other periods were better, and I fully respect that position. From my perspective, both musicians offered an important complementary role to the vocals, Jerry's guitar and the rhythm section of the band. Logically, they had to have if you focus in on how good the Dead were throughout the entire time these two were in the band. I saw some great show in the 1980's but, without a doubt, the concerts I went to in the 70's were the best. I've said this before on these pages.....Donna added something to many of the tunes Jerry and Bob sung. That female voice, when it was calm and softly sitting in the background, was an important element of what was going on throughout the bands prime years.

I just had to chime in on the review regarding 80s dead vs. this show.  While there are good shows from the 80s, especially 1980-1982, I just don't see how that period can even be compared to this stuff. 

Brent was definitely a talented player and singer but frankly the setlists suffered shortly after he joined the band and a couple years into the 80s Jerry went downhill (some combination of substance abuse and enjoying JGB more than the Dead I would guess).  Add the presence of Drums/Space in every show instead of good songs and they lost me for sure.  I always find myself skipping though shows after 1981 to find the "good stuff" while 70s shows I listen to all the way through.

I know there's an element of to each his own but you have to recognize that the furious pace of some early 80s shows was a result of cocaine and often times they were playing way too fast on some songs..so much so that they lost some of the feeling and Jerry 's throat was so numb he couldn't even sing a lot of the time.

This show is classic, tight, excellent Grateful Dead.  I generally prefer 1972-1975 but there is no doubting that the band was in a peak in 1977 and some of the shows are just unreal...including this one.

Whenever they played certain songs in '77 that were rare (TOO, PITB) they always played it with that extra oomph. 

And also I know what you guys are saying - I'm a huge Keith fan (not so much Donna) and the 70's are definitely their best decade, but I actually love at least a few shows every year, up until 1994 at least. Honestly I don't think these guys were ever weak at all. Certain times they were more on-point but literally every show I've ever heard, even the ones that overall weren't that great, still had at least one special moment.

Is it possible to get an audio hard-on ?

Recordings of this quality spoil you for everything else.

Thank you, Charlie. (And thanks for rattling the dust off the top of my sub woofer as well ! )  ;-)

This show has always had me come back for a listen. Whether the reggae-twanged early version of Jack A Roe, the soulful High Time, that bumpity Mexicali with Jerry philling in for Phil's backup vocals, or that intro jam into Eyes, this show is noteworthy for many reasons. 

To add my two cents to whatever was being argued or debated about Donna and Ketih's contributions verses Brent era stuff, I really think its futile to try say that either era was "better or worse". 

There are many gems hidden throughout the 80s that many 70s lovers would have dismissed and not listened to. 85', 87', 89', and 90' are all peak years and feature undeniably strong performances. But anybody who says that the Brent band was better than the Keith and Donna band is smoking too much DMT. It's just not a worthy tit-for-tat. The band was younger, more ambitious, and playing longer, more drawn-out jams in the 70s. 

If you don't like Donna's off-key vocals, then there is an argument to be made about how every member of the Dead really actually sucks at singing (none of them have traditional on-key vocals). And Keith did go downhill no-doubt (some shows from this month even display sloppy fills on his part) but listening to his contributions throughout the 70s, and the fact that Jerry had him as part of his band, show that they were integral to the scene, and not to be undermined. 

I almost like Keith's often submissive approach to playing, because it allows Garcia, Lesh, and drummers to play more furiously, and as for  "From the Heart of Me", I think we all deserved a bathroom break at some point, same goes for "I Will Take You Home". Snoooze.

I saw the review of the guy that said "no one under the age of 35 has ever seen the dead" -  TDCarowindz   You wanted to hear stories about road trips from those who actually saw the Grateful Dead with Jerry.  Well here goes......I started in 1973 when the Grateful Dead came to the Nassau Coliseum on Long Island.  In high school, I kept hearing about the 3 older students who became famous but went to our school.  Michael Hartman was one of those students (Mickey Hart). I won a raffle that year and the prize was Europe 72 so when the Grateful Dead came to the Nassau Coliseum I went to see them.....they appeared with NRPS on March 19th 1973 and the rest was history.  I spent 22 years on tour and 357 shows later with the full band in the USA - CANADA - AND THE SURROUNDING UNIVERSE.  The one thing I loved to do was to go see them on New Years in San Francisco.  I went every year during the Christmas and New Year's season in the 1980s.  I went for 5 years.   used to go whale watching first in Monterrey Bay for 3 days and then head to San Francisco for the shows.  In 22 years I have a lot of road trips stories (Hells Angels, Dead Heads out on parole from Folsom,  Cheysa Cheysa smokers from Shanghai, hot surfers from Monterrey Bay) Next story.....I added 2 other concerts over-seas 20 years after Jerry died....so my grand total is 359 concerts in 43 years......one of the 2 concerts was Mickey Hart and his band and then I saw a screening of the June 28th show from Santa Clara, California  Fare Thee Well 2015

reviews.reviewbody:
The Promised Land, Peggy-O, LLR. Estimated. Terrapin all were coming together nicely for Englishtown in Sept of that year. 
Great matrix. D. Latvala-> Charlie Miller is solid gold. PITB is scorching and tribal. Gigantic Sugaree!!

A show sitting in between several all-time greats, in possibly the greatest month, is going to be an unlicked cub. But it has its fans, and has a couple way-serious highlights. Even if not one of my usual suspects for May '77, I find I go back to this one sometimes. The show had been postponed from 4/20 (...pre-significance). First Set. The opener doesn't launch statim-strato like some shows from this month, but Keith is nice (and heard more clearly on the SBD). Well, this Sugaree has been much-discussed and almost defies non-Einsteinian consideration; like the speed of light for separate observers. A behemoth, with nooks and crannies of its own, it slows, it builds back, it breathes. The massive trip that occurs pours into the El Paso, and even the next two are above average. Row Jimmy is a bit sluggish, and a sloppy Passenger gets tighter halfway and feels safe-on-the-rails by the station (even sated). Just the third one, it's still getting wired up. Loser is a paragon, and when Dancing gets frothy it over-delivers. Second Set. Aside from highlights, the whole set is delish as played in context. P-l-a-y-e-d played. The opening sequence is cream May '77, finishing with a Samson that's the only song repeated from the night before. Terrapin & Playing aren't the best examples from the tour, if still quite good. Uncle John's is the show's low point. Keith provides the rectification for Jer to jump-start from the coda back in time to the intro, but they get a little lost a couple times. Drums are rarely exciting in this era, but as they resolve to The Wheel X factor re-emerges. This is only tight in a relaxed way, but that gives it individual charm. Some members test going back into Playing, but Jer starts teasing China Doll. The first since 10/74, there's some rust until it picks up for a great ending. The official release has an odd cut of 48secs @0:55 (because Jer kept slowing down, it causes an abrupt tempo change at the edit). At first, the Playing reprise is just Jer, Bobby and one drummer. It ends up sounding like a '72. They did not encore so it's a unique show-ender, but a bit of wandering through the desert before tidying up. 1st Set:  B 2nd Set: B Overall = 4 stars Highlights: Sugaree - behemoth Loser - paragon Dancing in the Street - gets frothy Samson & Delilah - so good Ramble On Rose - cracklin' Estimated Prophet - better than night before? Discuss The Wheel - individual charm SOURCES: The 139377_sbd_latvala is an upgrade; remastered and pitch-corrected. Except, weirdly, Dancing in the Streets is way too fast and needs -3% pitch. Or use bertha_9394 for that. Balanced and EQd, it has a better sounding 2nd set - unless you hold to the accuracy of the original tape. Dick's 29 has almost the whole show, and has a wider image than the SBD.

I like to think Ho Chi Minh would have been proud of that Peggy-O.

Other than that, insert generic comment about how great May 77 shows are and end it with "this more than meets the standards."

Woke up today and just had to hear this UJB. Wish I could tell you why but, honestly, who knows. Anyway, it really is a singularly great example of the band making legendary lemonade from life’s unpredictable lemons. Jerry playfully wanders (ok, charges full steam) into the UJB coda directly out of the Playing jam before singing the lyrics. Doh. 

The band briefly vamps as if looking at Jerry and saying:  “well, you got us into this, how you gonna get us out?” Jerry quickly improvises and, right on beat,  abruptly restarts the song. The band deftly follows, as if that’s how they always play the song. That moment, the seamless band interplay, and Jerry’s sharp solos are just brilliant, so much so you almost don’t notice Donna’s lyric flubs.  

Many debate which show in May 1977 is “the best” of all time (is it 5/8, 5/22, 5/28, etc). I don’t know if that’s even the right question, but I do know, this 5/19 show should, at a bare minimum, be included in any such discussion.
This show (among thousands) often peaks my interest for aLL of its flavor, but Today I heard a hint of exhaustion set over the band…

So, I'm checking out a bunch of Spring Tour '77 Scarlet Fires and I'm picking through other songs in the show I like and I come across this awesome They Love Each Other. Keith's solo is awesome. Also, this recording is crisp and full. Deep bass, you can hear every little drumstick strike of the bell of the cymbals. Just perfect. Row Jimmy starts off mellow but tight. Then it  rises at the first solo before returning to a mellow pace that rides a slow groove until the next solo. Overall, It's kind of soporific and reggae-ish but deliberate and controlled.Everyone is really listening to each other. Nice upbeat Passenger. Bobby's using the same effect he uses Dancin's from this period.Scarlet is just gorgeous. It's tight, mid-tempo. Everyone is playing together, all the little parts are nailed. Jerry and Donna's vocals are strong. It's probably as well-rehearsed as they would ever be. Studio dead live, sort of. The transition to Fire is beautiful. Pre-Fire transition solo by Jer is nothing special. He's just kinda doing little runs and trying to find something. It builds a little bit. But the thing is it kinda doesn't matter. The whole is greater than the sum of its parts. Everyone is playing so well, overall, And listening to each other that it becomes more about the ... whoa! Fire intro is fire! Mutron envelope filter here we come First solo is awesome! ! Mutron + distortion pedal! Yes!  There's a slight bit of Jerry's trademark pinch harmonic picking early on, too. There's a lot to like here. This Scarlet'Fire takes its time but there's a lot to enjoy here. Recommended!

reviews.reviewbody:
As the end was arriving me thinks to myself... Wow, that's a darn good Tennessee Jed! Its not exactly one of those songs you think of catching you, but when Jerry's playing the shit out of it... tis not to be denied! This show hadn't really caught my attention but decided to give it a chance as a result of a review I had read on another show page referring to this pair... Giving it four, only because its slightly less than the best of the others through this month of awesome shows, set-lists, and performances! And, again, the thing that caught my attention was the freakin' Tennessee Jed!
Good Grief! smiley faces for all!

Halfway between Kissimmee and Tampa, Lakeland had the 7000-seat Civic Center; but back then there was next to nothing in Kissimmee, and Lakeland functioned as an outer suburb of Tampa. Quite different today. This portion of the tour had been rescheduled, with this show moved from 4/15. In a way, this night is pointless to review. May '77 either means this or Barton, or Pembroke to most Heads. The band had an historic night, and everybody locks in on each song. I could pick any one and make an argument for year's best version. The first set alone is better than many well-regarded shows. The second set is an odyssey. First Set. A gleeful Bertha, an emphatic Me & My Uncle, a long-touted They Love Each Other and a slick Cassidy lead to an incredible two Jacks. The first, Jack a Roe features sinuous leads, and I like to picture Billy and Bobby both making cool-jazz-face. Jack Straw may not quite be 5/17, but the line of demarcation is already strung into the beyond, and when you're dealing with infinity it all becomes relative. Tennessee actually starts a bit too sluggish, but also blows wide. Row Jimmy is the set's low point. Ha! Low point! It starts with a good tempo and gets better and better. Passenger is potent and a gear-up to this very special Scar>Fire. The first is an ultimate, powerful version, the second comparable to 5/11, 5/12 & 5/17. Second Set. Almost every Samson in this year is great, but I'm going to argue that this is the best (on a given day I'd vouch for 2/27, 4/29, 5/17, 6/9 or 12/30). Context is part of it, because this leads into a Brown Eyed Women that may be the single best example. Bobby then pretends Jer (Phil?) is telling a joke while they make a setlist - some of this patter is cut from the official release. Estimated is also great all month, but this He's Gone is my favorite between 10/15/76>11/1/85. I can't say the same for Drums>The Other One, though it's well above average. The latter has a well-hidden reel flip @11:36 (the OFF instead has a cut @11:11 of 28secs). Comes a Time was never my fave (often a bathroom song), but - though it starts static - this is a definite keeper by the end. Some will say 5/8, but I prefer this St. Stephen>Not Fade Away as the best of the month (else 5/15). The funky era, there is just all kinds of goodness tucked inside. One More Saturday is exactly the right tone and mood, fitting the context of the set and happily exhausting. But you have to save some back for the gustatory U.S. Blues. It's so good the gods weep - shame they didn't stick this on DiP29; there was room. 1st Set:  A+ 2nd Set: A+ Overall = 5 stars Highlights: Whole show SOURCES: The 139573_sbd_gastwirt_miller is the remastered, pitch-corrected version, albeit some tunings have been trimmed. Dick's 29 has the whole show, except U.S. Blues and an edited TOO. It can use some balance and EQ intervention.
crisp sound, firing on all cylinders. just hearing this show for the 1st time on it's anniversary here in 2022, boy howdy! give er a listen!

Kord met a little mama and smoked all her hash then went into convulsions. Taco got busted by undercover for running 3 card monte. I was drinking rum from a pint I hid under my hat. Wanted to stay away from drugs and just enjoy the show. I think they did Rider before China. Someone said Captain Beefheart was in the audience.

...songs may end, but the experience remains. Try not to fight against the current. Instead, float down opposite aLL that is loose and free-flowing, as it cannot come with you after you've gone. It's cleansing and beautiful, actuaLLy, when you realize this with eyes open. Yet, many don't understand or pretend they don't notice as mounds of garbage pile themselves high above clouding heaven like towers destined to faLL under weight disguised. Practice acceptance, aLLow yourself enough love to see through empty darkness into the true nature. That is where we find our wisdom...

"mounds of garbage pile themselves high above clouding heaven like towers destined to faLL under weight disguised."
( self-piling garbage ...sounds good to me )
( heaven 'cloudy? ..must be the 'vapors'

Nick what the heLL are you babbling  about ? 

were you trying to write ''disgusted' -but became lexicon-ically challenged?

Did you forget your lithium ? heroin enema?

so glad you could take a break from sooth saying to write your startling insights on true meaning of garbage.
..........................................................................

my review- "great show, great recording.. thank you'

reviews.reviewbody:
Challenging trying to compare shows
 from the 1977 time period. 
Especially since Barton Hall
gets so much love and attention.
For me it is enough to compare 5/21 to 5/22.
I find I lean towards :
1st set of 5/21
over 5/22
but then I am partial to: 
5/22 Second Set over 5/21 Second Set.
H>S>F with an emphasis on Franklin's 
They play Samson, Be. Women both nights with 5/22 you get a stand alone Good Lovin
My reasons for at least the 5/22 Second Set are the Sunrise, Estimated > Eyes that is just enough to lean me towards 5/22 Second Set.
and then also how often do we get
Eyes Of The World-> Wharf Rat-> Terrapin Station-> Morning Dew, (4 to close from Jerry!)
oh yeah the transition out of Eyes is deeply moving. Almost could roll anywhere from a Dark Star to Stella but comes down on a Wharf Rat. (but really those  transitions always endeared me to this band. 
(Garcia said in the later years the most creative time musically was often coming out of space which is what the end of this Wharf Rat reminds me of)
The drummers really kick butt during Wharf Rat for a ballad the tension between Garcia and the Rhythm Section with August West goes in many possible directions! What  a great yet subtle drop into Terrapin. This is a bare bones version sans Lady with a fan.--starting with "Inspiration move me brightly"
I am surprised they never did just the Terrapin Station lyrics in the later years.( It might have cut down on a bunch of Jerry's having to remember both Lady with a Fan>plus Terrapin.lyrics which IMHO often slowed his guitar work.
Wow, into >Morning Dew. This is Jerry center stage vocally and of course jamming.
I guess it doesn't matter anyway!!! 
E) Sugar Magnolia-Well Bobby had to get him some as well.
For the record  -- i would still say that my favorite 1977 remains Englishtown 77.

I'll not comment on the performance here, because this show is widely accepted as one of the best performances of the legendary May 1977 tour -- if not *the* best, as I believe and as many others do as well.

Sound quality aside -- not bad for a cassette copy -- this is in some ways an upgrade to the commercial release. It's not just the obvious -- the 8 songs left off of Dick's Picks 3 are included --but also the less than obvious -- Eyes and Dancin' in the Streets, which were edited for DP3, are presented here in their complete versions.

No question, this show is right there among the best from this magical, mythical May of '77. Still remember first hearing the closing sequence (Jam->Wharf Rat->Terrapin->Morning Dew) on Gans' GD Hour back in the day. 

Official release cuts these from set one (El Paso, Peggy-O, Minglewood, FOTD, Ramble On), set two (B. E. Women, Good Lovin), and the encore (Sugar Mag).
The Grateful Dead

The trump virus 
Use the power 
Vote

reviews.reviewbody: Love this one, 5 stars fer sher
Not a song I'd normally comment on, but the High Time is exquisite!

despite the band seeming p.o.'ed at a late audience arrival, they hold it intact for a while and then explode in all of its frustration.

to fully appreciate this show back off the low end and elevate the gain.

beautiful hall ambience. remarkable.

brown-eyed, jack-a-roe, passenger,

high times in the ol' town hall

not a barn burner throughout but a keeper no doubt.

amazing remaster of a fanatical recording.

rates a 5 stars merely for overall sound and general enthusiasm.

Well played tunes thru the whole show. It's nice to hear a 77' show with a twist in the set list. I could do without Sunrise. Donna has really gotten better but that does not mean I want to hear her sing a song by herself. Overall 4 stars with Jack-o-Roe and High Time making the show a keeper

Don't knock on Sunrise! Donna's songs were great 77-79! From the Heart of Me and Sunrise might not be my favorite, but they are nice to year in the occational show to shake things up. I really like her voice in '77. St. Stephen, Not Fade Away, Estimated Prophet, Terrapin...I couldn't imagine those songs without her! Besides, I would rather listen to her solo songs than the cheesy 80's love ballads that Brent did! OUCH they suck ass! Far from Me, Easy to Love You...I have tried to force myself to listen to his songs the whole way through to see if I'm missing something. I always end up skipping the track a minute into it. His tunes fit in more with White Snake or something! 

This show is GREAT! May '77...you cant go wrong! Tight, full sounding band! FIVE STARS...INCLUDING SUNRISE! haha :)

Exellent both in performance and sound quality. Thanks Jay. This band played so many shows I could never rate any particular one as the best but I like this about as well as any of my personel favorites.

A motherfuckin' classic version of Sugaree. Orgasmic. Best version on the planet. Someone, tell me where I can find one better because I can't wait to listen to it through. And, for those of you that don't find much good in Donna, tune in to the background vocals here. There is no fucking way you will ever convince me that Brent did a better job. She had her good moments and some that were less than good. This is perfection. 

In fact, for what it's worth this was really a fine show.  If it was a 1976 or 1978 performance  many would say it was a standout. A truly outstanding recording.

Check out the Sugaree on Dicks picks Vol. 10. Its a winterland show on December 22, 1977 it is the same year and has this same vibe as do many 77 sugarees but the dicks picks vol. 10 version is more intense and jerry has much more raw emotion. The only part I liked more in this version is keith is more in the mix.

as far as im concerned you can keep Barton Hall ill take this one or the night before in Richmond anyday just a killer Music the Sugaree well im thinking its been covered on this page pretty well but smokin for sure ive always loved the 77 Jack-A-Roe's too. great show in a great month thanks Archives and especially Jay and Bertha

Whoa. Undoubtedly one of the tightest shows from the always tasty summer of 77. If you thought Barton was the peak of that month, behold what these gentlemen unleashed on Baltimore a few weeks later. The Sugaree is a jaw dropper - probably the best one I've heard. Jerry goes for it... to put it lightly. Set closes with a truly firemost Bertha. The whole band was on all cylinders this night; simply a must-hear for any fan of this exceptional period of Dead (frankly, who isn't?). Many thanks to Mr. Ashley for the exceptional mixdown - this special show got the magic touch =]
maybe my favortite May show still on the Archive. "Sugaree" is fantastic and "Terrapin" flavoured 2nd  is outstanding!

I was lucky enough to attend both the Mosque the night before and this one. 
What a blast, who would have know back then that these 2 shows were some the greatest performances the band put on. 
Thank You Band for the good times, Thank You Archives for letting me relive these moments and others.

Peace and Happy Holidays to All
Its time to legalize it this is my mantra for 2013.

Klearjet
reviews.reviewtitle: The most incredible 2 days of my dead life.

reviews.reviewbody:
Jay --

This sounds incredible.  Thanks!  Definitely allow Bertha to hang around.  

The playing is genuinely hot and the band is mixed very close to optimally:  You can actually hear Bob and he is really on.  If I had been mixing it I would have had Phil just a little bit higher, but this is about as good a mix as you are ever going to find.   Hearing the Jerry-Bob-Phil interplay is what throws my switch and you get some fine examples of it in Jack-A-Roe, Bertha, Brown-Eyed Women, Sugaree, to point a couple of songs out.
bertha solo is so complex and difficult to play. crazy how Jerry just rocks it out w no prob, thinking of it on the fly, taking me months to learn it...  amazing!!!
A peak performance from May 77. Grate show beginning to end, but this second set is exceptionally hot. Also, this recording is about as good as it gets. Enjoy this masterpiece.

in plain sight. Right at the end of a legendary run, between two released shows.

This one is right there. Such a clean recording of a great show.

As good as any pick IMVHO.

This one sure is, many great jams as referenced below and the sound quality and mix is truly outstanding.

Didn’t see anyone yet mention the GDTRFB & Around & Around. Both mighty fine. 

Chillin’ in the sun spinning this now, life is good.

Many thanks to the archive and all involved in bringing forth these treasures.

reviews.reviewbody: This is another one of them. I like the sounds that I've heard from "Bertha" very much. If you haven't already checked out this entire month, please do. This is a strong show, in my opinion. 4.5 Easy.

Dick was not impressed with this show, and it's nothing more than an average performance for May 1977. Other tnen what might be one of the all-time best versions of Sugaree, there is nothing distinguishing this show from any other from this period. Certainly there are numerous May '77 shows more worthy of official release. (92 pts)
can anyone hook me up with a copy of the bonus disk from the fillmore box set? if so i will get you copies of any soundboard on this site!! really any one.just e-mail me at
Of this beautiful Betty Board. It really shines, shines here. The other versions are a bit muffled.

The final show of the most-regarded tour is a hot, consistently above-average show with the requisite Spring '77 highlights - even if not one of the tours Top Ten shows! Not as constantly heated as, say, 5/21, 5/22 or 5/8 but still above-average with Garcia approaching differently than those dates. 1st Set:  B 2nd Set: B Overall = 4 Stars Highlights: Bertha - strong opener suggests strong show Sugaree - you may think it's peaked, but wait. A Top 10 of all time Minglewood Blues - so many good ones on this tour, but this is still a top 5 Samson & Delilah - Donna's great, everybody's tight Tennessee Jed - Jer is having an angular night and this version is loopy, close to jumping the rails until it scoops the corner Estimated Prophet - Donna on an on-night; edge of seat again One More Saturday Night - Jer still approaching from angles SOURCES: Ashley/Bertha of Betty Board & To Terrapin. But also check the Chappell matrix for N-R-G.

I remember seeing the boys here in the 80's and it was an interesting scene with Deadheads descending on the 
Hartford business district. Ever once in awhile getting a knowing smile from somebody in a suit and tie.
 If comparing it to the rest of this fabled Month of shows it is like 4 out 5 but that is with the seriously stiff competition of May 1977 still i prefer this to that stop and go Boston 77 show with all the hammering.
Garcia does extend in some interesting places like Sugaree and Tenn Jed.

reviews.reviewbody: Great show. Estimated Prophet all the way.
Love this version of China Doll. Great recording!
too bad no soundboards exists- great show!
Grate show. Grate setlist. Nice 2nd set.

So many great shows by numerous groups happened at The Forum in the 60s and 70s. It's such a legendary venue. This one flies under the radar because, afaik, it was not a traditional Dead venue, and as previous commenters have suggested, there aren't any boards. Mike Millard, The Forum's resident stealth taper also seems to have been absent from the proceedings.

That said, this is a damn fine audience pull. The sound quality gets consistently better. Early in the first set the sound is not as strong as in the later parts when is Phil laying waste to entire blocks of Inglewood. Be like the band. Be patient and let the show envelop you feel the sensation of the audience not giving up for the band, but expressing genuine please in the song selection and the moment they realize what they're hearing or about to hear, but also take note of the fact that many are likely hearing Terrapin, Sampson, and Estimated for the first time. I actually appreciate that the taper is not trying to shush everyone who tosses out a comment here or there. For the sound to be this clear, yet to feel so intimate with the audience as well is a real achievement. 'Cause, ya know, when the dude a few rows away yells out for Unbroken Chain, I'm like, right on, man, I'd take an Unbroken Chain right about now, too. Of course it doesn't happen, but what does happen is both hot and loose, but also patient and sensitive. Late spring '77 is a golden time for the Dead, from the north east shows to the Winterland run, so much good happening that a stop in L.A. is almost like a pit stop along the way. Judging by this recording it certainly wasn't a pit stop for the band. 

The first set rocks hard with a lot of energy. I mean, Brown Eyed Women and Jack Straw in one set, don't mind if I do. You can hear the appreciation of the crowd as they not, whoop whoop, but seem to collectively mutter "Oh, this is special," when they realize it's Friend of the Devil. This submission lists a track as "Space", but I don't think that was even a thing in 1977, was it? To me, that's just Franklin's jammin' out. 

The patient, open-eared transitions that don't simply run one song into the other, or stomp another out, but really take time to blend the nuances that make the transition possible are a treat. There are a few tape cuts. Not too bad. I could have used a bit more of the drum duel, for example, but there's nothing too jarring like a mid-phrase jump. 

It's a real gem, if ya ask me, which maybe you didn't.

reviews.reviewbody: This show is a great example of how the band was way more suited to having one drummer,has Mickey bangs away mindlessly and just clogs things up.

I wouldn't chose a 1977 show to try and pick on Mickey. He and Bill never played more in synch than this year after his hiatus. I don't hear any random drumming this show? Anyways.....

GREAT SHOW! Love from '77, killer Estimated, perfect Betty Board sound, too bad we are missing some of the first set. Don't let that scare you off!

re:- "never played more in synch" - that's the problem - duplication, two drummers playing more or less exactly the same. Maybe if Mickey had done something wildly different it (the drumming) would have been a bit more interesting. Why not three or even four (5, 6, etc.,) hammering out exactly the same? My drumming preferences? 1st - 'Live/Dead' era up to when Mickey left; 2nd - William 'Fairplay' on his own; last choice - this duplicated/plodding era.

But it's all personal opinion/preference. Whatever floats your boat ........
reviews.reviewtitle: Why not three (or even four) drummers ?

reviews.reviewbody: Jerry's Wolf comes back

Glad I downloaded this, and all other Betty's before Phil took them down, just recently rediscovered this show in a file that was buried in another file.  Anyway, this show is AWESOME.  Jerry's solo in Wharf Rat is unlike any thing I've heard him play before.  It's in a  higher note and hauntingly beautiful, very relaxed pace and just insanely sublime.  His voice really shines here too.  Probably my favorite version of my favorite song.   I'm listening an uncompressed file and my speakers have ribbon type tweeters that have come alive during this particular solo.

reviews.reviewbody:
Wild how @ about 06:18 into Let It Grow they let it flow into a Lazy Lightning jam. 

I am so glad life allowed us all to see them back then. And here here them again now.

Wunnerful funnerful sunnerful... beautiful.
reviews.reviewtitle: Oh man, Portland of a thousand jams

reviews.reviewbody:
right here in the PNW. 
it's so cool to to be able today to sit in the rooms where the boys played back then. to be able to visualize all that. the Warfield & such.

this Scarlet is gorgeously graceful.

If you ever have time to listen to youtube there is a thirty inute long "interview between Jerry and about ten other CocaCola Heads that say it is an interview but basically was just some cats that got backgstge with a tape recorder and a good amount of righteous blow, which you can hear them snorting every thity seconds like it's right next to the recorder and this is right before this show and jerry is tuning hihs guitar, they had not played Casey jones in some time and the fact that he was wired to the gills before he went out there (trust me listen to the tape) it is amazing that he has such a beautiful voice and pulls off the show flawlessly, right on Jerry, just wish you could have learned a little moderation and you might still be with us but everything happens for a reason.  rest in peace papa bear.
reviews.reviewtitle: Long May you run, listen to the interview or the before show pre-party on youtube and then dig this show! out of sight

reviews.reviewbody:
first set has a total of 21 minutes of nothing after songs.
music/transfer 5 star

There are half a dozen uploaded versions of this show. Ten songs were used by a biscuit company for their 'Flour Hour' of music on FM radio. That's all. 60 minutes. Others have offered us bits and pieces: set 2, the first set, etc., but now we have an imperfect, but welcome new version of this show. Even though there are large chunks of blank air after most of the first set songs, we can enjoy hearing most of this concert, and set 2 is great. DON'T MISS THIS!!!  One of the hottest--if not THE Hottest--Not Fade Away Jams ever played, can be heard in the second set. This is a must listen!

When I saw that Mr. Miller had kindly posted a “complete“ new version of this show, I decided to give it a listen, and I’m sure glad I did. Though its not regarded on the same level as many more well-known shows from May or fall 77, it is nonetheless mighty fine. The first set is fairly unremarkable, save the really nice Music Never Stopped to close it out. The second set, however, is a pure demonstration of raw power and ferocious playing by the band. See, e.g., the Estimated->Eyes. By the time they break into Not Fade Away the train is speeding so fast it’s hard to believe they not only kept it firmly on track, without careening over a cliff, but ably slowed things down long enough for a beautiful Black Peter which then, itself, gathered pace and rolled back into NFA. It should surprise no one that some thin lines of white powder just may have been involved. Regardless, the result all these years later is just another jolly good time and really fun listen. I must admit I nearly shed a tear when the tape runs out in the screaming UJB encore jam but feel so fortunate for what is here. See for yourself.

It takes awhile for the jam to kick in but once they find the sound after the rare 77 drums they are really lit 🔥
Good to hear Donna mellow on LLR and then hot on AROUND.
Enjoyable show for college heads at AZ
To me it is a Keith night as it is his key work that prods Garcia and puts this over the top.
Everthing sounds slow and sleepy, a good show to put on waiting for the Demerol to kcik in. But people love 77. Band could fart in a can and people would give it 5ers.

What took so long for this amazing show to get uploaded in completion?

Second set is ridiculous, esp NFA through the end. Enjoy the ride into the stratosphere. Holy Shit... 

BTW this "monkeytot" ass below me is a total suckbag
There's a brief, full-band 'Mind Left Body jam' just before minute 7 of the first part of Not Fade Away.

reviews.reviewbody:
this show rips. best night of this tour so far imo. keith, bobby n phil all shine thruout. jer n donna both have sum rough patches but overall excellent performances. excellent set list. peggy-o, dire wolf, estimated, eyes, dancin, nfa are all some of my favs of 1977 to this point chronologically. thought id miss keiths moog on estimated but the epiano sounds so dope snd his playing is phenomenal tonight. also keith, phil and bobbys chemistry on estimated is un real and then check out bobby n jerry on the dancin jam. also i think second set opener dancin is kinda rare placement? i think it was mostly late first set/set closer.
anyways great show. def worth a good listen.

Don't think for a second that anything from the fabled year of nineteen seventy-seven can produce anything lackluster. Nay, powerless - by the Grateful Dead.

This show came smack in the middle of their eight show Autumn southwest tour, which took them from Tempe, Arizona (October 6th) and ending in Baton Rouge (October 16th). The best parts of these shows are culled together on Road Trips Vol. 1 No. 3 for those interested. Where as many have been sought and contextualized as better than nothing's hidden away in Dick's Picks Vol. 29. Although, I believe a lot of this is overlooked because Englishtown (November 3rd, 1977) happened so thoroughly.

To cap it all off, the following week during their East coast Autumn tour would capture them in another syncopated extremely well-curated series of shows. 10/29 and 11/4 both postulate that nothing would ever come close to the riot that was the Grateful Dead.

Stadium shows and University tours in 1978 would go on to further explain that what they achieved on the aforementioned Fall tours in 1977 were sacred, especially now among the limitless Flac-trading communities of Now. I consider myself lucky to be able to hear these in startling quality, back-to-back whenever I'd like. Who is to say when and where these actually happened, although I am grateful to know (maybe) they did.

Back to the music at hand. What is shown here is above or slightly better than most of what can be heard. The opening trilogy Help/Slip/Franklin should not be missed, as well as the Dancin' In The Streets melody DIRE WOLF  AND  LET IT GROW. It's fire, absolute trench town Reggae. You won't regret a single moment if you ever could.

* Nick, 10/11/2023

reviews.reviewbody:
This recording reminds me of the way Professor Longhair would sound playing his wild New Orleans style piano.
I really like this recording!!!
Everybody has an opinion and a right to the same but it would seem to me that if you have listened to any amount of live dead this is on the higher end of the sound spectrum. 
(Well, then i get to Candyman and Garcia is low in the mix for vocals. Damn that sucks. Weir comes in clear on backing vocals. Augh! Donna Jean singing strong.
Not sure what happened to Garcia's vocals?)
Passenger-I like this tune, just a lot of moxy, 
never the same song without Donna Jean.
I always considered this a Phil tune 
even though he is not on lead vocals.
B.E. Women--- better on Garcia vocals.
Always one of my favorites.
Garcia's guitar work!!!
They get a little lost with the lyrics in Brown Eyed
No matter the tune has a life of its own.
El Paso-Maybe Bob a tad low vocally
but listen to Jerry's guitar.
Rhythm section.
F.O.T.D- Jerry pretty expressive on his vocals
Donna Jean just what Garcia needs on these slower Friend of the Devil's...
Great keys from Keith.
Lightning>Supplication-Another one of those tunes that was sorely missed in the later years.
"i need a double dose in any case"
Nice jam into Supplication!
Sweet Very Sweet Deal.

Samson-- Great GOD ALMIGHTY!!!
Tenn Jed,(76-77 they would put a normally 1st set tune in this slot, I like that it gives the set a little added flavor. Not sure they could ever equal the Europe 72 versions of this tune but they seemed to have a blast trying)
Estimated>He's Gone(Great harmonies)
(Brief) Drums >The Other One(slinky) ->
Black Peter(jam at end is EPIC)
 ->Truckin'(cuts somewhat)
 ->Nobody's Fault But Mine(this gets the funk meter) ->
Iko Iko (until I started listening to some of these recordings- I never knew what a treat AIKO was late in the 2nd set)->(transition from Aiko losses something with track break) to Sugar Magnolia (It takes them a few minutes into Magnolia before they break free of the IKO influence) It must have been something to listen to Jerry and the boys render this in 1977.
e) Johnny B Goode- A rockin version. Wow did the band give everyone their money's worth.
Encore fades out but i got the idea.

This sounds fine. Good show all around. Part of a great October 77 run of colleges. Next show at Hofheinz has a nice PITB sandwich which closes the show as second encore.
 I liked The TLEO and FOTD and the Lazy Supplication though short sounds tight. Second set takes off and Phil booms to begin TOO and booms again at the end of Truckin. Outro on Peter is fantastic too.
There was a fire in the meadow on the way to this show that had everyone park and walk.

reviews.reviewbody: long live the great humanitarian Charlie Miller!!

a nearly 6 minute Brokedown piqued my interest- some extra jamming, added lead break, spacey intro?
-Nyet, negative, nope. This sucker is half speed! Well maybe not half, but it's slow indeedy. Jerry plays a picture-perfect lead at the end, but besides that, if I had been there, I would have had trouble staying awake. SSSSLLLLOOOWWWWW.....
The Playin' reprise was a nifty little feature tacked on at the end, but I woulda been long gone!
Overall this show's average to above average for the era. Nice work on this matrix by the becoming-famous C.Miller elevates this one. Phil is a monster!

The Music Never Stopped, Playin' in the Band, and Wharf Rat make this a 5 star show IMHO.  CM...You are amazing.  Many released shows don't sound this good.  Thank you for this and all the many others.

Not sure why this AMAZING little item is available, but I suggest you GRAB IT WHILE YOU CAN!  

Thanks again, Mr. Miller!  If you snuck this one on, I salute you, sir.  Your heart and your ears are in the right place!
This friend of a devil is absolutely epic.  Bertha is excellent, and the whole playin sequence is pretty good.  Never really a fan of Around and Around though. <4.1 out of 5.>
Of course none of the other songs disappoint, but Friend of the devil in this set is absolutely spectacular.
love oct. 77'.this is why.

This show was the return to Houston, five years after the great '72 show, playing the Fertitta Center at U of Houston ('73 only saw an El Paso show and in '76 they didn't mess with Texas). First Set. After a solid opener, Mississippi Half-Step pushes toward X Factor. Except for some flubbed verses it's great; also one of the longest versions. On the official release the first 12sec are patched with 11/5/77. There's a great segue into El Paso. The second half of Brown Eyed pulls back, but Minglewood is all action, peak to valley. Loser is also a standout. Donna is good and the solo is gemstone. Bizarrely, the official moves the left channel to mono for the first 2 seconds, just to omit a muted strum from Bobby. Sounds like Jer says "let's try something else, like Bionic Man!" Did he mean Six Million Dollar Man? But alas, it's a rather flat Passenger. Friend of the Devil however is absolute kush on a tray. Everybody is ON, although Keith's solo is a bit buried. On Me & My Uncle in '77, Bobby went back and forth from "lyin' there" to "dead ass". Here it's the former - maybe because you get arrested in Texas. There are so many good versions of Music Never Stopped in '77, that even though this is awesome it's not among the best of the tour. Second Set. It takes a bit to get going, but when Jer takes off Bertha soars nonetheless. The next are a bit stumbly, with Candyman particularly sleepy (11/02 is the big one). Playin' has a nice breakdown section with some good Phil. The official version ends with a segue to another show, the fade out forgoing the last 20sec. The following few seem rote, into Wharf, where it suddenly goes technicolor. Then, Around & Around is a tempest version, with Jer meting molten movements onto the mountain. For the double encore, Brokedown is not the most un-sleepy, but Donna is good. The reboot Playin' though is a classic show-ender. The official release uses this as the bookend of a disc, just like the actual set, but artificially fills the middle with another show. 1st Set:  B 2nd Set: C+ Overall = 3½ stars Highlights: New Minglewood Blues - all action Loser - solo is faceted brilliance and Donna's good Friend of the Devil - everybody is ON Around & Around - tempest with molten movements Playing in the Band - nice encore tag SOURCES: The miller_110419 has fixed the dropouts and is complete, with good instrument separation (the beginning of ½-Step is clipped on all SBDs). The gorinsky_tetzeli_fix-6693 has more hall sound, less low end and separation, less distinct keys, less complete tunings. They are also two separate SBDs?! Three from each set are on Road Trips v1 #2, half of the six in unaltered form.
This show is lit. Really dug it.

this show rips start to finish. unreal second set. this brokedown is up there with winterland. some good tuning and banter. whole band isnfucking on. the few lyric flubs are nonissues. nothing catastrophic, excellent recoveries and performances do not suffer. top notch grateful dead, best show of the tour so far and probably at lwast top 10 of my favorite 77 shows.

reviews.reviewtitle: Texan first set, jammy second set!
reviews.reviewbody:
This is a very strong show. The first half of the setlist caters to the cowboys; it’s mostly rock, blues, and country. Very Texas. It’s crunchy stuff, and would definitely entertain any fan of that drum-heavy ‘77-’78 sound. 

After musically tipping their hat to their Houston hosts, they’re finally comfortable with uncorking some serious jam vehicles. Candyman is where they flip the switch, get trippy, and make this a whole different ball game. In Grateful Dead lore, Hofheinz Pavilion is best known for hosting one of the best ever Playing in the Bands back on 11/18/72. It is thus fitting that they would serve up another great PITB during their return to the venue five years later. The 10/14/77 Playin’ is certainly in the same league as its famous predecessor, although of a much different flavor stylistically. It sandwiches a great close to the show, reprising after a really extraordinary Brokedown Palace!

This is a wonderful ‘77 performance that showcases the Grateful Dead’s multifaceted musical machinations.

reviews.reviewbody: There are so many great shows in 1977 they almost start to seem routine, which is nuts. Anyhow, this is another terrific one, with numerous highlights, including a fiery 2d-song Sugaree (that first solo, whoa) and a raucous, set-closing Music Never Stopped, including fierce syncopation (starting around 4:30). The second set opens with a swinging Scarlet-Fire-Estimated suite and features a jaw-dropping, beautiful Black Peter that rivals any others, ever. The final, wailing solo (starting at 9:15) is simply spectacular. Now, go run and see!

reviews.reviewbody:
First off, thanks Charlie for another lovingly-restored BettyBoard.

There are a few rough patches -- most notably when Jerry couldn't quite find the phrasing in Stella -- but the Around & Around is one of the hottest I can recall having heard from any era whatsoever. Even Donna is uncharacteristically hitting her marks. She's downright unobtrusive, which is about the highest praise I ever give her. And the AUD patch at the end of the song adds a lot -- the one thing that can be missing from a 'board is hearing the audience go as nuts as you know they  must have at the end of something especially kickin' So...woo hoo!

One more thing: The mix on these old BB-sourced tapes should remind all of the Bobby-bashers out there just how critical he always was to the Dead sound. In this show -- as in so many others -- he's really the core of the song. the Casey Jones here highlights this beautifully -- Bobby makes the song. Check out his feedback/sustain at the end of Jerry's first solo (starting at about 3:03). It's F-ING BRILLIANT!!
Good show from a great year. Grate sound from C Miller like usual. If they hadn't played Sunrise I'd probably give this five stars.

reviews.reviewbody: And just about exactly perfect to play LOUD.
no track numbers, stream only.

"No labels" and "no track numbers" are not valid reasons for giving this show just one star, the lowest rating.

It's the music that counts and this is a five star show. OK, there are a couple of flaws e.g. start of "FOTD" cut and reel-lip in "Truckin'" but giving this one star is just plain ridiculous. I wish I could give it ten stars to cancel that out.

Also "stream only", if you believe that you'll believe anything ("you just have to dig around") and there's always Lossless Legs.

Get real njpg.
This one is an outstanding show and recording. The boys have it together and they seriously rock the Motor City. A definite add!

I was never a big Terrapin fan until I heard this one. Such a complex and deeply entrancing song. 
The whole set 2 jam from Terrapin>Estimated>Other One>Drums>Wharf Rat is just gorgeous. 
I'll take any recommendations for other late 70s shows like this.

Excellent sound quality. 
And those that complain about stream-only shows need to get over their desire to own things. Just my opinion.

reviews.reviewbody: I've been making my way through each show from '77 and just got through this one.  I'm surprised it isn't considered one of the top shows of the year.  It's a real underrated gem.  Sound quality is excellent too.   Check it out if you haven't yet.
Top to bottom well played.  No Highlights.

Cobo Hall was famous as a heartland metal/hard rock venue. The Dead only played it twice, after this casting about for various south MI venues before committing to Pine Knob in the '80s, and The Palace in the '90s. Maybe not the best show of the tour, but the focus is on the top of the second set – a must-hear sequence. First Set. Might as Well works nice as an opener, though they are still warming up. Jack Straw kicks it open and has a nice feel. The next few are average '77 [that's always good!]. The beginning of Friend of the Devil is missing about 1½min. Jer emphatically adds his conversation to Looks Like Rain, but the drummers have been out of synch this whole set. After a perfunctory Dire Wolf, Mickey[?] says "play Yellow Bird" (re a version of Choucoune by Arthur Lyman), Jer takes a stab, Billy[?] says "that's pretty". Passenger and Peggy-O are yr average. After an attempt at a Funiculì, Funiculà tuning, Music Never Stopped is one of the strongest of the set, perfect for the break. Second Set. Terrapin to open? Without warning, this is something extra; punchy, with extra little bits from each player. They know it, because that lift-off then buoys Estimated (feels so much like it was gonna be a Playin'). The mutron jam section is as good as other top '77s. The tether threatens to snap on the awesome tranny into The Other One, which then bumps against the universe. After Drums, Wharf Rat has two nice jams but sluggish verses. Truckin' has a reel flip @2:16, missing ~25secs. The end of the short set drops off with a flat Around and a shoes-in-dryer U.S. Blues. 1st Set:  C+ 2nd Set: B- Overall = 3¼ stars Highlights: Terrapin Station>Estimated Prophet>The Other One - big lift-off sequence SOURCES: The miller_82574 is great (adjust for balance, EQ and low volume).

reviews.reviewtitle: That transition into The Other One!!!
reviews.reviewbody: Worth price of admission alone. Estimated>Other One always had potential. Powerful! I've seen it done with other bands to good effect. Nice Fall 77 jam here.

My CD copy of this show has always been a real favorite. Nice clear sound, great song list. The real break between sets is after Let It Grow,  as BW announces (“so hang out”). reviews.reviewbody: This is one of my favorite shows from 77!

Great Half Step opener 
with Garcia getting some on the extended jam.
Mellow Jack Straw chaser
In fact everything about 1977 is pretty much laid back
except when they go into jam mode
then the contrast is stunning.
I love Donna Jean's vocals 
integrated into the music.
She sounds good here!
also she shines on any JGB 
I can get my hands on from this time period.
Take a step back,,, I heard that at a few shows
but no clue which ones they were.
General Admission often the issue.
I liked GA because it took the ushers out of play
but the magnetic draw of being up front
"like a moth before a flame"
Tenn Jed-easy to take this for granted
After Europe 72 this song an uphill battle
but was fun live for dancing and yes swooning.
Great sound on this recording 
most of the comments are on the other Soundboard.
Switched over to other soundboard now back 
for Dire Wolf. 'Don't Murder me"
Another one of those tunes 
I often forget about when making up fantasy set lists.
In 1978 they slightly revamped this tune and just nailed it.
this is a good version, sing along material.
Pretty creative 1st set list and a Music Never closer
"High Stepping into town"
Bobby with some lyric malfunctions
Here comes Garcia!
A nice 8 minutes of MNS...

Samson
"It being Sunday we are going to do a little tune of spiritual derivation" -Weir
Nice Samson, Can't go wrong with Samson & Delilah 
Sunrise-I like Donna Jean so I dig this tune
She has a great voice.
When we head outside the Garcia and Weir Universe
Tunes like Sunrise add another dimension
 to the GD songbook
Can you answer > = < YES i can
St.Stephen>Drums>N.F.A>Wharf Rat>Stephen>Truckin' E) Johnny B
Truckin' as 2nd set closer anytime!!!
It has that little extra umppphhhh.
closer mojo...
Johnny 'B' great for an encore
ensemble singing at its best.

Went to 11/5/77 in Rochester! Best show I ever attended! Listening to this show--it is close! Garcia is on fire for the whole show--incredible! Dead Heads--don't underestimate these shows--they are the best of the best!

This whole year is just awesome. (My first show was Englishtown in Sept. 77, so I may be a little biased!) Like the best Wharf Rats out there, it builds beautifully then explodes gloriously. The whole band kicks it out, and Jerry's guitar at the top just gave me chills.

reviews.reviewbody: I try to stay away from reviewing performances as it is such a subjective topic, but sound quality....good god this one is crisp! A million thanks to the people that make this stuff available.

Nov & Dec '77 was one of the hottest periods; a string of 8 incredible shows. 11/4 & 12/29 are astonishing and the NYE run is probably the best one overall. It's particularly known for 12/30, one of the best shows of all time. But the shoulder shows are are also worth hearing. This show is better than NYE itself and, though not as good as the next two, is as good as 11/2 Toronto & 11/5 Rochester. And, did you note the Samson as encore? The original circulating SBDs have a censored Wharf Rat and are missing the encore. First Set. The verses are flubbed for Bertha but the solo is insane. Good Lovin' is beautiful, just not tight. That changes for the exciting Brown Eyed Women. Listen to Bobby's rhythm and Keith, both beyond the call of duty. The Cassidy is hotter than soup, and Jer uses that advantage to make emphatic statements. Most of the rest is average '77, though with the shoes creeping into the dryer by Passenger. After Candyman, Bobby apparently makes a comment to the drummers, who in return threaten to take Bobby's watch. "They're criticizing your watch Bob!," Jer teases. Friend of the Devil is the best of the rest, though Music Never Stopped leaves 'em happy for the break. Second Set. Cold Rain & Snow is tight enough, but very straightforward. Seems like a 1st set opener. The last minute of Supplication is where things get hot again. Take your protein pills and put your helmet on for this Scarlet Begonias. The verses are great and I dig the lolloping solo, and love the little bits alongside the jam into Fire. The jam from Estimated>He's Gone is also nice, but Truckin' takes a powder. Wharf Rat is pretty rote until the jams, which turn over pebbles and find rocks. Clunky set finisher Around & Around is ameliorated by a one-of-a-kind encore Samson that brings the Xfac back one more time. 1st Set:  B- 2nd Set: C+ Overall = 3¼ stars Highlights: Brown Eyed Women - rhythm guitar great, Keith great Cassidy - Jer's emphatic statements Scarlet Begonias - lollops and extras [you'll probably want to check off Samson-as-an-encore, too] SOURCES: A Miller source finally appeared, without the censored Wharf Rat and the digital glitches in Lazy Lightning, and with a patched Around and with the encore! The sound quality is superb (though the channels are reversed and it needs boosted highs for the second set). If you compare the glitch in Lazy Lightning in the Ashley_Bertha source to the redbeard_3989, you'll hear the amount of reverb and EQ often coloring the Bertha-processed sources

Quality 12 30 material. ever heard a bad 12 30 show? 
Not I. Maybe some other band.

Always really fine shows at year end. This is a perfect example of nice set list,top playing by Weir, of course Jerry,and the rest. There are standouts, but I wont start a long,long review,we all have our preferences.
Try Nov. and Dec.of 71’ Pig, and the band are incredibly tight, and John Cutler at the time was producing shows with clear crisp sound. Love those shows, but here is a show 6 years later with the same drive and force as almost always! 
Keep the mother rollin………

reviews.reviewbody: Great set list and inspired rock n roll.

This is really good. Nice to hear all the DP 10 outtakes. My favorite show that I have personally attended and of all the recorded history I have experienced. 

Especially love it how they come out of the PITB Jam. Jerry was jumping around on stage, windmilling fat chords at the ending ala Peter Townshend of Who fame.

This is a sweet reminisce of a rainy night at Winterland when everything was "just exactly perfect."

Thanks to Charlie Miller for the resplendent remix and kudos to the Archives.org.

Just want to agree with Evan Hunt that this too is my favorite of all the shows I saw ('75 - '95). And YES! Jerry literally DANCING on stage. I always tell folks that and they don't believe me. 

A very special night and rare that 12-29 was not the night off. It was originally booked as a three night run. When they added the fourth show (27th) they needed a night off (28th). In '79 it started to be the norm to play 12-26, 27, 28, (29th off), 30, 31. Just a little nerdy trivia for ya.
This. When the aliens get here, and for those living here, we give u this on behalf of us humans, as our leaders (the band) are best at communicating what we all want to say. Thanks for listening.

if there was ever a run of shows that I would have most liked to attend. the joy running through these boards sounds absolutely insane!

edit;  after very dedicated listening, I've come to the conclusion that while this jam is really interesting, and definitely worth hearing on a few occasions, there are other things worth spending your time perusing. Jerry's tone in Fall 77 and Spring 78 (into the later part of the year) is really fabulous...enjoy!

Comments:

From Alan

"I transferred these masters direct to untracked CDs back in 2002. I checked them out and they are spot on for speed (A=440). It seems to be a sort of sbd/ambient blend mix to mono. The masters were labelled as "Remote" so I'm assuming its a unique mix of some sort, possibly as the feed to video cameras. It sounds similar to the audio on Bill Graham's video masters but is superior quality and more complete. It may be the most complete direct source as it does not have any of the cuts on other sbd sources. The only cut is during the tape change in set 2 (during the jam after Truckin')"


SIRMick

I have compared a couple of tracks with the mix used for Bill Graham's video at the Convert Vault and can confirm that it is  the same as this.


Notes:

- The audience which has been mixed in is rather excessive during  Set I so I have toned it down so that it isn't so overpowering.
- I put together a matrix to patch "Jam'" which is a 100/50 mix of shnids 20596 and 140952 (Thank you Brian Heath, Matt Smith and Scott Clugston).    Both sources were speed corrected and some level adjustments made. I made this mono so that it is in keeping with the rest of the source.  The patch is



Thanks to Bob Gurman for this source and Alan Bershaw for the transfer.



edited and masstered
SIRMick
April 2018

reviews.reviewbody: This is a smoking hot show and cannot believe no one else has reviewed this... half step one of the best ten jed playin - long really trippy with a great loop back around and triumphant close and this is the first set !!! Second set is really really hot with a close of terrapin - crowd is really into it and sound not all that bad if this were a mint board it gets a 5....
reviews.reviewtitle: Sound quality and splicing little dodgy however....

reviews.reviewbody:
This is a must must have.  The crowd is so into it and wild and crazy I felt like I was right there.  The yelling the screaming...the crowd signs half step for Jerry.  Kinda cool to hear a gap in the lyrics filled by the crowd (and not because Jerry forgot the words.)

Every song is fantastic.  I just about lost it at the end of Playing, just way too fantastic.  Solid show all the way through.

Sound somewhat less than desireable, but you forget about it quickly enough.  Get this one!
reviews.reviewtitle: Let me tell you how good this show is

reviews.reviewbody: Certainly is nice to hear Jerry jam in this show's Fire.  Very cool.  Thanks Jer.
Killer show.  Not sure why the SBD isn't listed here.  Too new, perhaps...

Great Scarlet>Fire, the guitar and harpsicord notes just rock and sway in a manner unusual for even 77-78; but the kicker is Peggy-O when Keith lays down some solo bass notes on piano near the closing refrain, second to last one I believe in an extrodinary display of classic ballad playing that shows how gentle he really was.

Of course the Half Step rocks with the Philly audience chanting along in the old house where the acoustics are as fine as any indoor arena. Long live the Spectrum Shows and this one is for Mike and Phil 'cause you know who you are....

MY REVIEW BELOW IS RELEVANT EXCEPT FOR THE FACT THAT A COMPLETE SOUNDBOARD IS NOW AVAILABLE AT THIS SITE. SCROLL DOWN TO THE LAST PHILLY ENTRY FOR THE SOUNDBOARD VERSION OF THIS SHOW. An excellent show. It was the first concert in what must be known as the best East Coast tour of the post-retirement version of the Dead. All of that precise playing and energy of the March Winterland run a month before continue in this show: the still sweet Jerry vocals and much varied guitar work/sound, a lively Keith, and a prominant Phil all held together by Phil and Micky at their best (of course, Donna and Bob are no slouches either). Fine as almost every show was all the way through June 9, it is true what many Heads have noted through the years--that some of these shows were technically perfect but just not incredibly interesting, with repeated setlists and similar approaches to the extended medlies. This Philadelphia show was certainly VERY interesting (as was the next, great show in Springfield). Just one of those nights where the familiar sounded new. Take the 21 minute Playing. Post 1974, I find that usually Playing should have been called Meandering in the Band. Not this one; it brought me back to 1972 with it's speed and intensity. Cool Keith sounds, a great Jerry crescendo at the ten minute mark, and a triumphant ending (enhanced by the audience recording, which is fine except for some chatter doing the quiet parts; indeed if the Playing was a soundboard, Heads would surely rank it very high on the list). The soundboard acceptably covers set 2 with the exception of Roses (excellent by the way...has a solo which was lacking pre-retirement). Look out for the second ever Fire...very bouncy and different than any other I've heard; no lyrics until the fourth minute. And the Dancin' through Terrapin is intense with those dancing beats bouncing away into a stately transition to a Wheel and then a powerful show closing Terrapin. The fun part about the audience portion is to experience the energy of the band in '77 from the audience perspective. And on this night the band was as good as they would ever be in that pinnacle year of 1977.
What a killer Estimated.  I think this may be my favorite version of it ever!

first show after high school with a high school friend i rarely saw anymore. ate some crummy acid that kept things just weird enough throughout the show. 
our first listen to terrapin "what the fuck is this?!" with garcia rocking out, actually moving around and getting down, DOWN like almost to his knees. then...
zip. 
slap.
house lights up.
no encore.
"what the fuck was that?!"
Very nice show, excellent roses...
Was this the fist time they were played in this sequence?

...the best part of this incredible Spring '77 show.  It's got to one of the following:  (1) the sick, stand-alone (and long) Playin' to close the first set; (2) Scarlet>Fire (especially the "Fire" portion of the transition and Fire proper); or (3) Dancin' > Mojo > Dancin'.  I give up since they are individually and collectively awesome.  So many other great renditions as well, including Peggy-O, Ten Jed, Estimated, Roses and Terrapin.  This one is a true Jerry-fest!!
Just read the reviews while starting off the set!! Can't wait to rock to the whole thing while working on the Friday morning in So Cal!!!

reviews.reviewbody: Wow - you REALLY gotta want this one.  It may be the only recording available from this show, but that doesn't mean you need it.  This is a poor quality audience recording - almost unbearable.  The performance is nothing special, either.  Get the nights before and after before even considering this one!!

Get this and find out.  Whoever said this a "one star" show is prolly accustomed to perfect sbds.   This has occassional chatter, but the sound is FANTASTIC all things considered.   This is the same source that was used for that DVD/VCD partial that circulated some time back, and the sound is soytainly worth a listen.  Check out the grooves eminating from Dancin !!!
reviews.reviewtitle: How did it sound in 1977 from the FRONT ROW ?

reviews.reviewbody: Though its a bit chatty at times, once you see the DVD of this performance it makes it much more appealing.  Anyone interested in giving the video portion of this show a shot, email me and we can set up a trade.  All in all a nice DVD/VCD to go with the show.

Estimated Prophet.  
http://video.google.com/videoplay?docid=-7263265928266920275
Lots of things to see. Bob in beard.  Travis Bean guitar.  Moog keyboard.  Donna restrained.  Mickey, Bill, Keith and Phil trying to get a little air time.  Jerry is having a great time on his solo.
reviews.reviewtitle: check out his little video bit from the gig

reviews.reviewbody:
on night four of the tour, conserving our energy it seems. nice venue more than makes up for it.

first set pretty laid back, and the song selection pattern never quite gets the energy up and builds to any kind of crescendo.  (4-way, my ass!  if i see that guy outside...) save for an energetic big river (nice work, keith!) and an ever-improving estimated (cool sound, jer!)which i really dig in the first set position, a competent but otherwise very forgetable set.  

second set not much different.  nothing, save the dancin' stood out for me.  a week from now after the nyc run, i don't expect i'll even remember what they played tonight with looking at my crib notes.

tomorrow i'm going stone cold sober.  maybe a night off will do the trick?  

-----------------------
note to LMOTs*:  the band members don't play differently because you call their names, yell song titles or go all beatles-teeny-bopper-orgasmic with your repeated "oh my gods" during a song.  save the inane yacking for after the show - did you come to listen or to blab? 

simple equation: mic + taper + your promximity to same = shutyourmouthanddance.  

no wants to hear you in the first place, much less for eternity.  

*LoudMouthsonTour

Well played 77 first set. 1/2 Step shines but not quite later 77 versions. Seems if the focus of the night is the HOT Dancin. Put some headphones on and do it. The sound is so so but I can hear everyone doin their thing at about 9 mins. Jer breaks out the slide! Wow. In the groove. Need a Miller of this show. Quality 77

The "DVD"/video is the only thing that makes this show worth collecting (& even that is questionable) because of the poor audio quality.
Find/Get the 19770427 video(s) instead!
The video quality is the same, but the setlist & audio qualities are MUCH, MUCH better ...

This was my second Dead show. 15 years old and took trains and busses from Queens to Passaic. Missed the last bus and was stranded until the morning. Parents not happy! For me this was a magical show. Maybe not one of the best 77 recordings but still I guess it was one of those shows you had to be at to understand. Sometimes I like aud recordings like this that make you feel like you are back in the crowd.

This is NOT a terrible AUD recording as some may suggest. No, it is not a crystal, clean "Betty Board" nor a prime front-of-the-stage mike job. But it is all here. There is a little "warble" at times, but you have all the instruments and vocals. Very listenable, but perhaps not at high volume. AUD recordings are nice to give you sense of the ambiance in the house that night.
Not a bad recording.

I don't write many reviews because everyone has their preferences in what defines a good show. But after seeing the poor reviews and inaccurate descriptions I felt inclined to give my two cents worth. 

Most folks on the Dead sites know me as a soundboard whore (which I am) but this is a great Aud recording, especially given the date and equipment available at the time. Huge thanks need to be given to all those that took their time, money and efforts to record these shows on their own accord for us to enjoy decades later. 

Recording Quality: low signal to noise ratio, very little distortion, good recording level across the board, no wavering, fluctuations or tape issues - it's a solid 8/8.5 sonically 

As for the show itself, it's not a barn burner nor top-lister by any means but a handful of songs are definitely worth an ear; Bertha, Estimated, Dancin', Eyes, and especially Stella, Jer closes the show strong.

Peace,
Audiohead22
reviews.reviewtitle: Some nice highlights worth giving an ear

reviews.reviewbody: unhearlded Gem here, the sound picks up about half way thru.  The Dancin thru Stella Blue are as good as it gets grateful dead. if this were a betty board it would be a beloved show. one of the few tougher to find shows from the tour.  If a snbd I would possibly go the extra star

I am going through DAT tapes and transferring all to HD before the tapes become unplayable. Just spun a copy of this show but the tape ends abruptly after Sugar Mags. 

In researching whether anything was missing, I of course checked here and etree.org, looking for all copies in existence. This copy with the Lazy Lightning encore here is incorrect.

Several offers of proof. 

1. DAT tape from 1999

2. http://db.etree.org/shn/260

COMMENTS No encore. (1) Dancing In The Street is not reprised at the end.

RECORDING AUD 150 with the beginning of Bertha clipped and minor cuts in Tennessee Jed. 
Source: Teddy GoodBear AUD Front Row Center

3. From the original tree source (linked in the description ironically): http://www.goodbear.com/tree.html

Source: Panasonic AM/FM Stereo 'boom box like' w/condenser mics) > CM (Cassette Masters) > various equalizers & editors > CD or DAT   

4. From the "Official" video that exists here:

https://youtu.be/oktHSQTUbGE?t=1h34m51s

Note how heads are waiting with bic lighters. Waiting for an encore that never comes. Finally the video shows people leaving.

5. Lazy Lightning has never been played as an encore or without being followed by Supplication.

6. If one downloads the Lazy Lightning encore from this listing, it becomes obvious that this was filler of some sort from the April '77 run. Possibly other stuff, but the lazy Lightning and anything after is included here erroneously. 

Just setting the record straight here as many people's only interaction with the Dead or downloading/ streaming shows is the Archive Project.

For whatever reason, it appears there is no known source besides the Teddy Goodbear and that has been heavily edited to make it listenable. Perhaps with the new batches of Betty Boards that are surfacing, we will get another gem.

The video is really cool as well. 

I will post another source from the original DATs shortly.

One final point: I was involved in treeing these tapes back in the day and remember some of the names you still see (how crazy is it these pages still exist?) 

Kudos to everyone that made this happen back in the day and peace and love to everyone that hears the fruits in years to come.

THERE WAS NO ENCORE on 4/26/1977! lol

Peace.
Good show. It almost sounds like the band is playing a bar. Dancin' is the highlight of the show.
reviews.reviewtitle: Frankentrack at the end is a mix of an AUD from 5/8/1977

reviews.reviewbody:
this show is phenomenal. the recording is frustrating at times but not awful. good crowd but some frustarting chatting/screaking next to kics at points.
but wow what a hot show. first set is phenomenal. high energy, tight, beautiful playing from the get. 1st uncle of the year. beautiful roses.q donna is flawless tonight. her tone, pitch, resonance and just so in it. she makes cassidy for me and delivers dancin. 2nd cassidy of the year, this one is beautiful and tight. jerry is on fire and him and bibby go off on dancin. bobby unfolds a bit more on good lovin tonight and sets the pace for the second set. i like the second set half step, it really takes off. and the rest of the second set it unreal. jerrys voice is so acute and expressive.
this is probably gonna stay in my top shows as i go thru the year. definitely a keeper and hopefully a better tape surfaces someday.
